Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q01 Scenario: A student is preparing a presentation about source evaluation. Which choice best shows a clear perspective and coherent focus? \

answer.text: A. The presentation states one clear point about source evaluation and uses details that support that point.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: B. The presentation lists several unrelated school topics.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. The presentation uses a decorative image with no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. The presentation avoids stating what the audience should understand.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q02 Slide note: A student wants to support a presentation about revision clarity. Which slide note is most audience-ready? \

answer.text: A. Lots of stuff about revision clarity and other things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: B. A copied paragraph with every source detail on one slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. Concise evidence connects revision clarity to the presentation perspective.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: D. An unrelated sentence that does not support the message.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q03 Speaker note: A slide gives a short point about peer feedback. Which speaker note best explains rather than repeats the slide? \

answer.text: A. I will read the slide exactly as written.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: B. This slide is here because it is on the screen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. Now I will talk about a different topic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. This point matters because it helps the audience understand how peer feedback supports the overall message.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q04 Revision task: Which change would most improve clarity for a presentation about \

answer.text: A. Replace vague wording with precise language that names the communication purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: B. Add more unrelated facts to make the slide longer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: C. Remove the perspective so the audience can guess the point.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. Use smaller text so a paragraph fits on the slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: A. Check only whether the slides have colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: B. Confirm that slides, speaker notes, evidence, and wording support the same audience-focused message.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

answer.text: C. Add new unrelated content at the end.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: D. Ignore conventions and source reliability.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This choice weakens the communication task because it is vague, unsupported, unrelated, or not audience-ready.

answer.text: A. I will read the slide exactly as written.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q09 Claim: Students should use a planner to manage assignments. Which evidence best supports the claim in an oral presentation? \

answer.text: A. Some planners have colorful covers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail may be true, but it does not show how planners help manage assignments.

answer.text: B. Many stores sell planners in August.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This fact does not explain why planners help students manage assignments.

answer.text: C. A teacher reports that students who write due dates down are more likely to submit long-term assignments on time.

feedback.text: Correct. This evidence connects directly to assignment management and comes from a relevant school source.

answer.text: D. A student says notebooks are heavy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support the claim about using planners to manage assignments.

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q10 Readiness check: Which final check best prepares a presentation about audience awareness for an audience? \

answer.text: A. Confirm that slides, speaker notes, evidence, and wording support the same audience-focused message.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice applies the Unit 6 communication skill accurately and keeps the presentation focused for the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q11 Digital presentation purpose: Explain how weekly planning helps students manage assignments. Which slide should come first? \

answer.text: A. A final thank-you slide

feedback.text: Incorrect. A thank-you slide belongs at the end, not before the audience knows the perspective.

answer.text: B. A random image of a backpack

feedback.text: Incorrect. An image without purpose does not establish coherent ideas.

answer.text: C. A slide stating the topic and clear perspective

feedback.text: Correct. A digital presentation should begin by orienting the audience to the main idea.

answer.text: D. A list of unrelated homework complaints

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not introduce a clear presentation focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q12 Perspective: Source checks help students choose stronger research evidence. Which slide note is clearest? \

answer.text: A. Stuff about sources and research

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is vague and would not help the audience understand the evidence.

answer.text: B. Check author, date, and purpose before using a source.

feedback.text: Correct. This slide note is concise, clear, and connected to the presentation perspective.

answer.text: C. Sources can be on websites and in other places.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is broad and does not explain the source-checking strategy.

answer.text: D. Research is something students do in school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general and does not support the specific perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q13 Slide note: Revision improves clarity. Which speaker note best supports the slide? \

answer.text: A. Revision improves clarity because the slide says it does.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only repeats the slide without adding explanation.

answer.text: B. Revision is a word on this slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the meaning of the slide.

answer.text: C. I will read the slide now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reading the slide aloud does not add meaningful oral explanation.

answer.text: D. Revision helps writers make ideas easier to follow by improving word choice, transitions, and explanations.

feedback.text: Correct. This speaker note explains the slide instead of simply repeating it.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q14 Scenario: A student will speak to classmates about why everyone should bring a notebook to advisory. What is the speaker's main purpose? \

answer.text: A. To entertain classmates with a funny story

feedback.text: Incorrect. The scenario does not focus on humor or storytelling; it asks the speaker to explain why classmates should do something.

answer.text: B. To summarize a long article about notebooks

feedback.text: Incorrect. No article is being summarized, and the task is about preparing an oral message.

answer.text: C. To compare several school supplies

feedback.text: Incorrect. The scenario names one action, bringing a notebook, rather than comparing multiple supplies.

answer.text: D. To encourage classmates to bring a notebook

feedback.text: Correct. The speaker is trying to influence classmates to take a specific action, so this identifies the purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q15 Scenario: A student is preparing a short presentation for school administrators about adding more quiet study space after school. Which language choice best fits the audience? \

answer.text: A. Additional quiet study space could support students who need focused time before leaving campus.

feedback.text: Correct. This wording is formal, specific, and appropriate for administrators.

answer.text: B. Quiet rooms are awesome and everybody knows it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too casual and unsupported for school administrators.

answer.text: C. We need more places because students are tired.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not clearly fit a formal school audience.

answer.text: D. People should just let us study somewhere.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sounds informal and demanding instead of audience-aware.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q16 Scenario: A speaker wants to use reliable evidence about online research habits. Which source is most credible? \

answer.text: A. A random comment that says research is annoying

feedback.text: Incorrect. A random comment is not a reliable or valid source for a presentation.

answer.text: B. A school survey that reports how students evaluate websites for assignments

feedback.text: Correct. A school survey is relevant and provides evidence connected to the topic.

answer.text: C. A meme about students copying information

feedback.text: Incorrect. A meme is not strong evidence for an academic oral presentation.

answer.text: D. A friend's guess about how many students check sources

feedback.text: Incorrect. A guess is not reliable evidence because it is not based on clear data.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q17 Topic: classroom discussion. Which sentence gives the clearest oral presentation perspective? \

answer.text: A. Classroom discussion is the topic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only names the topic and does not give a focused perspective.

answer.text: B. Classrooms have discussion sometimes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a vague detail, not a perspective.

answer.text: C. Classroom discussion helps students understand texts because they hear and explain different interpretations.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear point of view and explains the focus.

answer.text: D. I will talk about discussion for a while.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names the activity but does not state the speaker's point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q18 Presentation purpose: Show a problem and then recommend a solution. Which structure fits best? \

answer.text: A. Compare-contrast

feedback.text: Incorrect. Compare-contrast is for similarities and differences, not mainly problem and solution.

answer.text: B. Random order

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random order weakens coherence.

answer.text: C. Problem-solution

feedback.text: Correct. This structure matches a presentation that identifies a problem and recommends a solution.

answer.text: D. Alphabetical order

feedback.text: Incorrect. Alphabetical order usually does not build meaning for this purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q19 Which evidence source is most credible for a digital presentation about student research habits? \

answer.text: A. A random anonymous comment online

feedback.text: Incorrect. Anonymous comments are difficult to verify and are weak evidence for an academic presentation.

answer.text: B. A school survey showing how students choose online sources

feedback.text: Correct. A school survey is relevant and provides evidence connected to the presentation topic.

answer.text: C. A friend's guess about research habits

feedback.text: Incorrect. A guess is not reliable enough to support a digital presentation.

answer.text: D. A joke about students searching the internet

feedback.text: Incorrect. A joke is not reliable research evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q20 Which slide note is best for an integrated oral and digital presentation? \

answer.text: A. Feedback reveals unclear claims.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: B. A long paragraph with every planned sentence

feedback.text: Incorrect. Slides should not carry the whole speech.

answer.text: C. Stuff about feedback and writing

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague to guide the audience.

answer.text: D. I will say something here.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not communicate a useful idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q21 Scenario: Topic: school clubs. Audience: ninth-grade students. Which sentence states the clearest perspective? \

answer.text: A. This presentation is about school clubs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only names the topic and does not give a clear perspective.

answer.text: B. There are many different school clubs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fact-like statement, but it does not show the speaker's point of view.

answer.text: C. School clubs happen after school on different days.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives a detail, not a focused perspective.

answer.text: D. Joining a school club can help ninth-grade students meet people and feel connected to school.

feedback.text: Correct. This is a focused point of view that can guide a presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q22 Scenario: A speaker is addressing parents about student organization habits. Which phrase uses academic vocabulary appropriately? \

answer.text: A. Staying on top of stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is conversational and vague, so it does not fit academic speaking well.

answer.text: B. Doing things better

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is too general and does not clearly communicate the idea.

answer.text: C. Developing consistent organization routines

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase uses precise academic vocabulary appropriate for a formal audience.

answer.text: D. Getting it together

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and would weaken a prepared oral presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q23 Which order is strongest for presenting oral information with evidence? \

answer.text: A. Claim, reason, evidence, explanation

feedback.text: Correct. This order helps listeners understand the point before hearing and interpreting the evidence.

answer.text: B. Evidence, unrelated detail, claim, joke

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order is confusing and includes information that does not support the claim.

answer.text: C. Source title, source date, closing sentence, claim

feedback.text: Incorrect. Source information alone does not create a clear oral sequence.

answer.text: D. Explanation, new topic, evidence, claim

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order delays the claim and interrupts the focus with a new topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q24 Perspective: Weekly planning helps students manage long-term assignments. Which detail best supports the perspective? \

answer.text: A. Some planners have spiral binding.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is about a planner's design, not how planning helps students manage assignments.

answer.text: B. Many students carry backpacks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This may be school-related, but it does not support the planning perspective.

answer.text: C. Students sometimes talk in class.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unrelated to weekly planning and assignment management.

answer.text: D. Long-term assignments can be divided into smaller tasks across several days.

feedback.text: Correct. This detail supports the perspective by showing how planning helps.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q25 Which slide sequence is most coherent? \

answer.text: A. Funny image, thank-you slide, problem, title

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order confuses the audience and delays the focus.

answer.text: B. Title and perspective, problem, solution, final takeaway

feedback.text: Correct. This sequence builds a clear idea in logical order.

answer.text: C. Solution, unrelated quote, title, random fact

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sequence does not develop one coherent idea.

answer.text: D. Final takeaway, title, unrelated image, problem

feedback.text: Incorrect. The final takeaway should not appear before the audience understands the presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q26

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q26 Weak slide note: The research source thing is helpful because people can see whether source stuff is good. Which revision is clearest? \

answer.text: A. People can look at the thing and know stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is still unclear and informal.

answer.text: B. Source stuff is good for many things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This remains vague and does not improve clarity.

answer.text: C. Research is research when people research it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is circular and does not explain the idea.

answer.text: D. Source checks help students judge whether evidence is reliable.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision is concise, clear, and uses precise language.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q27

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q27 In a presentation, the word "credible" means which of the following? \

answer.text: A. trustworthy and reliable

feedback.text: Correct. In this context, credible evidence is evidence the audience can trust.

answer.text: B. confusing and unsupported

feedback.text: Incorrect. Credible information should be clear and supported.

answer.text: C. colorful and decorative

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color and decoration do not determine credibility.

answer.text: D. unrelated but interesting

feedback.text: Incorrect. Interesting information is not necessarily credible or relevant.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q28

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q28 Scenario: A student plans to explain recycling rules to new students. Which planning note best includes purpose, audience, and perspective? \

answer.text: A. Recycling rules are posted near the cafeteria.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is only a detail and does not include the full speaking plan.

answer.text: B. New students need to hear a presentation in the cafeteria.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names an audience and place but does not state a focused perspective.

answer.text: C. I will explain to new students how following recycling rules keeps shared spaces cleaner.

feedback.text: Correct. This note includes purpose, audience, and a clear perspective.

answer.text: D. My topic is recycling at school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only names the topic and leaves the purpose and perspective unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q29

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q29 Scenario: A student will speak to classmates about using a homework checklist. What is the clearest purpose? \

answer.text: A. To describe every assignment from the week

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would list information, but the scenario focuses on a checklist habit.

answer.text: B. To explain how a checklist can help classmates manage homework

feedback.text: Correct. This purpose fits the audience and explains what the speaker wants listeners to understand.

answer.text: C. To entertain classmates with a story about homework

feedback.text: Incorrect. Nothing in the scenario suggests the purpose is entertainment.

answer.text: D. To compare school rules from different classes

feedback.text: Incorrect. The task is about a homework checklist, not comparing rules.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q30

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q30 Claim: Quiet study spaces help students complete work. Which explanation best connects evidence to the claim? Evidence: The library sign-in sheet shows more student visits during project weeks. \

answer.text: A. The library has tables and chairs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This describes the place but does not explain how the evidence supports the claim.

answer.text: B. More visits during project weeks suggest students seek quiet space when they need focused work time.

feedback.text: Correct. This explanation connects the evidence directly to the claim.

answer.text: C. Project weeks happen during the school year.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This repeats a basic detail without connecting it to student work.

answer.text: D. Students sometimes like going to the library.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not explain the specific evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q31

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q31 Perspective: Students should use study groups before quizzes. Opposing view: Some students learn better alone. Which response keeps coherent focus? \

answer.text: A. Studying alone is boring, and school lunches should change.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This dismisses the opposing view and shifts to an unrelated topic.

answer.text: B. Study groups are always perfect for every person.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too absolute and does not fairly handle the opposing view.

answer.text: C. Quizzes are sometimes difficult.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is related to school but does not respond to the opposing view.

answer.text: D. Some students do learn well alone, but study groups can still help students hear explanations they may not create by themselves.

feedback.text: Correct. This acknowledges the opposing view and returns to the main perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q32

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q32 Which slide note best fits an expository digital presentation? \

answer.text: A. Step 1: Identify all due dates for the week.

feedback.text: Correct. This note clearly explains one step in an organized process.

answer.text: B. Due dates are annoying and nobody likes them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and not explanatory.

answer.text: C. I do not know what the next slide is about.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This shows lack of organization.

answer.text: D. Look at this unrelated picture.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q33

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q33 Which phrase uses academic vocabulary appropriately for a slide about evidence? \

answer.text: A. pretty good source stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is informal and vague.

answer.text: B. random facts from somewhere

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase suggests weak evidence and lacks precision.

answer.text: C. credible evidence from a reliable source

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase uses precise academic vocabulary appropriate for the topic.

answer.text: D. things that help maybe

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is too uncertain and unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q34

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q34 Which slide note uses standard English conventions? \

answer.text: A. Revision helps writers make ideas clearer.

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence uses correct subject-verb agreement.

answer.text: B. Revision help writers make ideas clearer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The verb does not agree with the singular subject "Revision."

answer.text: C. Revision help writer's make ideas clear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This has agreement and apostrophe errors.

answer.text: D. Revision helping writers make ideas clearer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment rather than a complete sentence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q35

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q35 Scenario: Audience: school administrators. Topic: adding a tutoring table after school. Which wording best fits the audience? \

answer.text: A. We really need this because students are stressed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is understandable but too general for an administrator audience.

answer.text: B. An after-school tutoring table could provide targeted academic support for students who need help before going home.

feedback.text: Correct. This is formal, specific, and appropriate for administrators.

answer.text: C. Tutoring is a thing people probably want.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal, so it weakens the message.

answer.text: D. Everybody should just agree to make tutoring happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sounds demanding and does not show audience awareness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q36

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q36 Scenario: Topic: reading before bed. Which sentence is a clear perspective statement? \

answer.text: A. Reading before bed is the topic of my presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only names the topic and does not state a perspective.

answer.text: B. Many books can be read at night.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a general detail, not a guiding perspective.

answer.text: C. Some people read and some people do not.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a vague observation and does not guide a presentation.

answer.text: D. Reading before bed can help students create a calmer routine before sleep.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence gives a clear point of view about the topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q37

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q37 Claim: Students should learn how to evaluate online information. Which reason best supports the claim? \

answer.text: A. The internet has many colors and videos.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This observation does not explain why evaluation skills are important.

answer.text: B. Some websites have short paragraphs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Paragraph length does not prove that evaluation skills are needed.

answer.text: C. Students need to know whether online information is trustworthy before using it in assignments.

feedback.text: Correct. This reason logically supports the claim and prepares for credible evidence.

answer.text: D. Online information is easier to copy than textbook information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support responsible evaluation of sources.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q38

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q38 Which phrase uses academic vocabulary best in a focused oral presentation? \

answer.text: A. stuff I want to say

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is informal and vague.

answer.text: B. a bunch of school things

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is too general for academic speaking.

answer.text: C. talking about whatever

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase shows lack of focus and inappropriate vocabulary.

answer.text: D. coherent presentation focus

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase uses precise academic vocabulary connected to the lesson skill.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q39

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q39 A digital presentation has slides about planning, cafeteria menus, sports scores, and homework. What is the main issue? \

answer.text: A. It has too few colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The main issue is not design color.

answer.text: B. It lacks coherent ideas because the slides do not support one perspective.

feedback.text: Correct. The topics are disconnected and do not build one clear message.

answer.text: C. It uses no paragraphs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Slides should not rely on long paragraphs.

answer.text: D. It needs more unrelated slides.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More unrelated slides would make coherence worse.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q40

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Question ID: ENG1_U06_UA_Q40 A slide has a full paragraph of evidence copied onto it. What is the best revision choice? \

answer.text: A. Add another full paragraph to balance the slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. More text would make the slide harder to read.

answer.text: B. Remove all evidence from the presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence is still needed; it should be presented clearly.

answer.text: C. Use a concise evidence note on the slide and explain the evidence orally.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the slide clear while preserving the support.

answer.text: D. Make the paragraph smaller so more words fit.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Smaller text does not solve the clarity problem.
